name: A whole day, outside and inside
summary: An editable day with a workday portal, parallel responsibilities, interruptions, recovery, and tomorrow’s preparation. Elevation distinguishes focus, coordination, and recovery; times are examples.

name: An application through many reviewers
summary: A learning-budget application moves through intake, completeness, manager review, budget review, coordination, decision, and fulfillment. Rework and decline paths are explicit. This is an illustrative process, not an organization policy.

name: Plan a household week
summary: Shared commitments, meals, errands, home and work tasks, exceptions, and reflection. Editable checklists help turn the model into a planning conversation rather than a prescribed routine.

name: Home and neighborhood
summary: Start outside with a family, home, shop, and bus. Click Home to enter its rooms while the neighborhood stays dimmed. Illustrative capacities, not measurements.

name: Family morning
summary: A household morning: waking, washing, breakfast, study, and departure. Objects describe people, furniture, food, and the relationships between activities.

name: Outside and inside the office
summary: View the workplace from outside, then click the office to enter a shared workspace. Desks, seating, windows, and shared facilities remain ordinary inspectable objects.

name: Daily commute
summary: Compare walking, bus, and rail legs on a daily journey. Optional in/out capacities distinguish a small walking route from larger shared transport links.

name: Family trip
summary: Follow a family from home to airport transport, a flight, and a place to stay. An illustrative travel structure with bidirectional route capacities.

name: Retail operations
summary: Follow customers, products, shops, and fulfillment across three planes. Includes a custom parcel-locker model alongside the built-in business objects.

name: Event launch
summary: Map an event from its people and ticket offering to registration, confirmation, and channel notifications. A business and communication model.

name: Order approval workflow
summary: Follow a request through validation, human approval, an API call, an event, and notifications. Includes a custom Approval type that reuses a built-in shape.

name: Three-tier web application
summary: A familiar web stack: browser, reverse proxy, application, relational data, cache, and background e-mail. An editable reference pattern.

name: Multi-tenant SaaS
summary: A shared application with explicit tenant context, identity, subscription billing, and asynchronous notifications. Illustrates shared infrastructure, not a complete tenant-isolation design.

name: E-commerce platform
summary: A storefront with catalog, cart, checkout, external payment processing, and asynchronous fulfillment. Service boundaries are illustrative and can be consolidated.

name: Background job processing
summary: An API and scheduler feed workers through a queue, with retry and dead-letter paths. Useful for document conversion, reports, and long-running tasks.

name: Headless content publishing
summary: Editors publish through a CMS while an independent delivery frontend consumes a content API. Media uses object storage and a CDN; publishing jobs refresh delivery artifacts.

name: Real-time collaboration
summary: Two real-time servers share durable messages and fan-out work while clients keep WebSocket connections. Includes presence, attachments, and offline notifications.

name: Analytics data pipeline
summary: Operational events and batch extracts flow through ingestion, raw storage, transformation, and a warehouse to dashboards. A logical reference for analytical workloads.

name: One request across service instances
summary: Trace a request across an edge, three alternative application instances, shared data, asynchronous workers, and exceptions. Branches are routing alternatives; not every instance executes every request.

name: Umbraco local Cluster
summary: The checked-in Umbraco demo: CM + two CDs, YARP, SQL-backed cache, shared filesystem media, and Aspire tools. Local development; the Astro frontend is independent of Umbraco.
